scenes.heading: Income and wages
scenes.say: A café worker is paid by the hour, a teacher earns a salary, and a real estate agent earns commission. Let's learn to work out pay every way, so you can check a payslip and compare jobs.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A taxi meter ticks up for every minute you ride
scenes.science: A wage adds the hourly rate for every hour worked
scenes.breaks: A salary isn't a meter: it is a fixed yearly amount, split into equal pays.
scenes.say: A taxi meter ticks up for every minute you ride. A wage works the same way: every hour adds the hourly rate to your pay. Overtime is like the late-night rate, when the meter ticks faster. But a salary isn't a meter at all. It's a fixed amount for the year, split into equal pays.

scenes.heading: Ways to be paid
scenes.say: A wage is the hourly rate times the hours. A salary is divided by fifty-two for weekly pay, twenty-six for fortnightly, or twelve for monthly. Commission is a percentage of sales. And net pay, what reaches your bank, is gross pay minus deductions like tax.

scenes.heading: Normal hours plus overtime
scenes.say: Dan earns thirty dollars an hour for a thirty-eight hour week, and works forty-two hours. First the big bar: thirty-eight normal hours, eleven hundred and forty dollars. Then the overtime piece: four hours at time-and-a-half, forty-five dollars an hour, which is one hundred and eighty. Gross pay: thirteen hundred and twenty dollars.
scenes.caption: Dan earns $30 an hour for a 38-hour week and works 42 hours. Normal pay: 38 × $30 = $1140. Overtime: 4 hours at time-and-a-half, $45 an hour = $180. Gross pay: $1320.

scenes.heading: Penalty rates
scenes.say: Time-and-a-half means multiply the normal rate by one point five, so thirty dollars becomes forty-five. Double time means times two, so thirty becomes sixty. Only the extra or weekend hours get these rates.

scenes.heading: Comparing two jobs
scenes.question: Job A: $68 640 p.a. Job B: $34 an hour, 38 hours a week. Which pays more per week?
scenes.say: Job A pays sixty-eight thousand six hundred and forty a year. Job B pays thirty-four dollars an hour for thirty-eight hours. Change both to weekly. A is thirteen hundred and twenty. B is twelve hundred and ninety-two. So Job A pays twenty-eight dollars more each week.
scenes.caption: Job A: $68 640 a year. Job B: $34 an hour for 38 hours. Weekly: A is $1320, B is $1292. Job A pays $28 more each week.

scenes.say: Quick recap. A wage is rate times hours. A year has fifty-two weeks, twenty-six fortnights and twelve months. Time-and-a-half is times one point five, double time is times two. Commission is a percentage of sales, and net pay is gross minus deductions. Now try the practice questions!
